diagnostics.notes: Both claims verified against their abstracts. A: HR 1.06 (95% CI 0.91-1.22) per 1-SD total dairy, authors conclude no major role for dairy in T2D prevention after MI. B: RR 0.97 (95% CI 0.95-1.00, P=0.04) per 200-g/d total dairy, significant inverse association. Same exposure (total dairy), same outcome (incident T2D), both association-type contrasts. A reports an explicit no-association conclusion against B's reported inverse effect, so the not_replicated branch applies with priority over apparent_contradiction; the population difference (post-MI patients vs healthy adults) is noted but not used as the deciding factor.

source_evidence.quote: After adjustment for confounders, including diet, HRs per 1-SD were 1.06 (95% CI 0.91-1.22) for total dairy, 1.02 (0.88-1.18) for milk and 1.04 (0.90-1.20) for yogurt.
Our findings suggest no major role for dairy consumption in T2D prevention after MI.
Total dairy was inversely associated with T2D risk (RR: 0.97 per 200-g/d increment; 95% CI: 0.95, 1.00;P= 0.04;I(2)= 66%)

verdict.label: not_replicated
verdict.rationale: Both findings concern the association of total dairy intake with incident type 2 diabetes. Abstract A (post-MI cohort, HR 1.06 per 1-SD, 95% CI 0.91-1.22) explicitly concludes 'no major role for dairy consumption in T2D prevention after MI' with absent associations across dairy types. Abstract B (meta-analysis of healthy adults) reports a statistically significant inverse association for total dairy (RR 0.97 per 200 g/d, 95% CI 0.95-1.00, P=0.04). One source explicitly reports no association while the other reports an effect, so the pair is classified as not_replicated; the differing populations (drug-treated post-MI patients vs healthy adults) are a plausible contextual difference but the explicit no-effect conclusion takes priority.
